en istap.explanation: "En istap" means "an icicle". It is built from "is" (ice) and "tap" (a peg). The part "is" also appears in "en isbjørn" (a polar bear).

en isterning.explanation: "En isterning" means "an ice cube". It is built from "is" (ice) and "en terning" (a cube). To talk about a die in a board game, the same word "terning" is used: "Jeg slår med terningen" (I roll the die).

en isvaffel.explanation: "En isvaffel" means "an ice cream cone". It is built from "is" (ice cream) and "en vaffel" (a waffle). To offer someone an ice cream, say: "Vil du have en is?" (Do you want an ice cream?)

en italiener.explanation: "En italiener" means "an Italian". To describe food or other things, use the matching word "italiensk": "italiensk mad" (Italian food). The same word names the language. To say you speak it, say: "Jeg taler italiensk" (I speak Italian).

en iværksætter.explanation: "En iværksætter" means "an entrepreneur". It is the noun for the verb "at iværksætte" (to set going). To say what someone does for a living, Danish leaves out "en": "Hun er iværksætter" (She is an entrepreneur).

et ildfast fad.explanation: "Et ildfast fad" means "an ovenproof dish". It is "et fad" (a dish) with the adjective "ildfast" (fireproof) in front. The part "ild" (fire) also appears in "en ildslukker" (a fire extinguisher).

et imperium.explanation: "Et imperium" means "an empire". The shorter word "et rige" (a realm) is also used for an empire. To name the Roman one, say: "Romerriget" (the Roman Empire).

et indbrud.explanation: "Et indbrud" means "a burglary". It is built from "ind" (in) and "et brud" (a break). The part "brud" also appears in "et benbrud" (a broken bone). To say a burglary has happened, say: "Der har været indbrud hos naboen" (There has been a burglary at the neighbor's).

et indkøb.explanation: "Et indkøb" means "a purchase". It is built from "ind" (in) and "køb" (purchase). To say you need to buy groceries, say: "Jeg skal lave indkøb" (I need to do the shopping).

et indkøbscenter.explanation: "Et indkøbscenter" means "a shopping mall". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "et center" (a center). The word "et shoppingcenter" (a shopping mall) means the same.

et indlæg.explanation: "Et indlæg" means "a post / contribution". To talk about something you publish online, say: "et indlæg på Facebook" (a post on Facebook). To say someone gives a short talk at a meeting, say: "Hun holdt et indlæg i mødet" (She gave a talk at the meeting).

et indtryk.explanation: "Et indtryk" means "an impression". To say something affected you strongly, say: "Det gjorde stort indtryk på mig" (It made a big impression on me). Do not mix it up with "et udtryk" (an expression). To talk about a phrase, say: "et sjovt udtryk" (a funny expression).

et initiativ.explanation: "Et initiativ" means "an initiative". To say someone is good at starting things, say: "Han har meget initiativ" (He has a lot of initiative). To say you did something without being asked, say: "Hun gjorde det på eget initiativ" (She did it on her own initiative).

et insekt.explanation: "Et insekt" means "an insect". It is the first part of "et insektbid" (an insect bite), built from "insekt" and "bid" (a bite). To say you have been bitten, say: "Jeg har et insektbid på armen" (I have an insect bite on my arm).

et instinkt.explanation: "Et instinkt" means "an instinct". To say someone is naturally good at something, say: "Han har et godt instinkt for fodbold" (He has a good instinct for football).

et institut.explanation: "Et institut" means "an institute". At a Danish university, a department is called "et institut": "Institut for Datalogi" (the Department of Computer Science). A beauty salon is "et skønhedsinstitut" (a beauty institute).

et instrument.explanation: "Et instrument" means "an instrument". To ask whether someone plays music, say: "Spiller du et instrument?" (Do you play an instrument?) To talk about a tool for measuring, say "et måleinstrument" (a measuring instrument).

et interview.explanation: "Et interview" means "an interview". To say you interview someone, use "at interviewe" (to interview): "Journalisten skal interviewe ministeren" (The journalist will interview the minister). For an interview for a job, use "en jobsamtale" (a job interview): "Jeg har en jobsamtale i morgen" (I have a job interview tomorrow).

i.explanation: "I" means "you". To speak to several people at once, use "I" as the subject: "Er I trætte?" (Are you all tired?) Do not mix it up with "i" (in), which sounds the same: "i huset" (in the house).

i aften.explanation: "I aften" means "this evening". To say what you will do later today, say: "Jeg ser en film i aften" (I am watching a movie this evening). To talk about the evening that has already ended, use "i aftes" (last night): "Jeg så en film i aftes" (I watched a movie last night).

i aftes.explanation: "I aftes" means "last night / yesterday evening". To say what you did the evening before, say: "Jeg så en film i aftes" (I watched a movie last night). Do not mix it up with "i aften" (this evening), which is the evening still to come: "Jeg ser en film i aften" (I am watching a movie this evening).

i dag.explanation: "I dag" means "today". It is written as two words, unlike the English word. Literally, it is "in day". To ask what someone is doing today, say: "Hvad skal du lave i dag?" (What are you doing today?)

i det hele taget.explanation: "I det hele taget" means "on the whole". To say you like something in general, say: "Jeg kan i det hele taget godt lide det" (I generally like it). To ask whether something is possible at all, use it in a question: "Kan du i det hele taget svømme?" (Can you swim at all?)

i det mindste.explanation: "I det mindste" means "at least". Literally, it is "in the smallest". To say something is still good in a bad situation, say: "Hun er syg, men hun har i det mindste ikke feber" (She is sick, but at least she has no fever).

i det store hele.explanation: "I det store hele" means "all in all". Literally, it is "in the big whole". To sum up your overall view even though some things were bad, say: "I det store hele var turen god, men hotellet var dårligt" (All in all the trip was good, but the hotel was bad).

i eftermiddag.explanation: "I eftermiddag" means "this afternoon". To talk about the afternoon in general, say "om eftermiddagen" (in the afternoon): "Jeg læser om eftermiddagen" (I read in the afternoon).

i forgårs.explanation: "I forgårs" means "the day before yesterday". It is built from "for" (before) and "går" (yesterday). To say the same thing with a number of days, say: "Det skete for to dage siden" (It happened two days ago).

i forhold til.explanation: "I forhold til" means "compared to". To say something is cheap or expensive next to another thing, say: "Det er billigt i forhold til Paris" (It is cheap compared to Paris).

i fortiden.explanation: "I fortiden" means "in the past". It is built from "i" (in) and "fortiden" (the past). To talk about what comes later, use "i fremtiden" (in the future): "I fremtiden bliver det nemmere" (In the future it will be easier).

i forvejen.explanation: "I forvejen" means "beforehand". To say you do something before the time comes, say: "Du skal bestille bord i forvejen" (You need to book a table beforehand). To say you already have or know something, it means "already": "Jeg kender hende i forvejen" (I already know her).

i fremtiden.explanation: "I fremtiden" means "in the future". It is built from "i" (in) and "fremtiden" (the future). To talk about the time before now, use "i fortiden" (in the past): "Det skete i fortiden" (It happened in the past).

i første omgang.explanation: "I første omgang" means "at first". It is built from "i" (in), "første" (first) and "en omgang" (a round). The word "omgang" also means a round of drinks. To say you will buy the next round, say: "Jeg giver en omgang" (I will buy a round).

i gang.explanation: "I gang" means "on", as in a movie that has started and is still running: "Filmen er i gang" (The movie is on). To say you get started, use "komme" (to come): "Vi kommer i gang klokken ti" (We get started at ten). To say you start a project, use "at sætte" (to put): "Han satte projektet i gang" (He started the project).

i gang med.explanation: "I gang med" means "busy with". To say what you are busy with right now, put "er" (am / is / are) before it: "Jeg er i gang med lektierne" (I am busy with the homework). To name an action, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Hun er i gang med at ringe" (She is in the middle of calling).

i går.explanation: "I går" means "yesterday". To say which part of yesterday you mean, add a time of day: "i går morges" (yesterday morning).

i hvert fald.explanation: "I hvert fald" means "at least". To say something stays true whatever happens, it means "in any case": "Jeg kommer i hvert fald" (I am coming in any case).

i kraft af.explanation: "I kraft af" means "by virtue of". To say a job or position gives someone the right to do something, say: "Hun kan beslutte det i kraft af sin stilling som formand" (She can decide it by virtue of her position as chair). To give an ordinary cause such as weather, use "på grund af" (because of): "Vi bliver hjemme på grund af regnen" (We are staying home because of the rain).

i lige måde.explanation: "I lige måde" means "likewise". Literally, it is "in equal way". To return a good wish, answer with it: "Hav en god dag!" "I lige måde!" (Have a good day! You too!) The part "lige" also appears in "lige nu" (right now) and "lige meget" (it does not matter).

i mangel af.explanation: "I mangel af" means "for lack of". It is built from "i" (in), "en mangel" (a lack) and "af" (of). To say you accept something because nothing better is there, say: "Vi tog bussen i mangel af bedre" (We took the bus for lack of anything better).

i mellemtiden.explanation: "I mellemtiden" means "in the meantime". It is built from "i" (in), "mellem" (between) and "tiden" (the time). To say what someone can do while waiting, say: "Maden bliver færdig om ti minutter, så i mellemtiden kan du dække bord" (The food will be ready in ten minutes, so in the meantime you can set the table).

i modsætning til.explanation: "I modsætning til" means "unlike". It is built from "i" (in), "en modsætning" (a contrast) and "til" (to). To say two people are different, say: "Han er rolig, i modsætning til sin søster" (He is calm, unlike his sister).

i morgen.explanation: "I morgen" means "tomorrow". To say what you will do the next day, say: "Jeg tager til Aarhus i morgen" (I am going to Aarhus tomorrow). Do not mix it up with "i morges" (this morning), which looks almost the same: "Hun ringede i morges" (She called this morning).

i morges.explanation: "I morges" means "this morning". To say what you did earlier today, say: "Jeg læste avisen i morges" (I read the newspaper this morning). Do not mix it up with "i morgen" (tomorrow), which looks almost the same: "Jeg har fri i morgen" (I am off tomorrow).

i nat.explanation: "I nat" means "tonight / last night". To talk about the night that has just passed, say: "Jeg sov dårligt i nat" (I slept badly last night). To talk about the night to come, say: "Jeg sover hos Anna i nat" (I am sleeping at Anna's tonight).

i nærheden.explanation: "I nærheden" means "nearby". It is built from "i" (in) and "nærheden" (the nearness). To say what the place is near, add "af" (of) after it: "i nærheden af banegården" (near the train station).

i og med.explanation: "I og med" means "since". Literally, it is "in and with". To give a reason that is already known, add "at" (that) after it: "I og med at det regner, bliver vi hjemme" (Since it is raining, we stay home).

i orden.explanation: "I orden" means "all right". It is built from "i" (in) and "orden" (order). To tell someone an apology is fine, say: "Det er i orden" (That is all right). To say papers are correct and complete, say: "Papirerne er i orden" (The papers are in order).

i overmorgen.explanation: "I overmorgen" means "the day after tomorrow". It is built from "over" (over) and "morgen" (tomorrow), so it jumps over tomorrow. To say the same thing with a number of days, say: "Det sker om to dage" (It happens in two days).

i princippet.explanation: "I princippet" means "in principle". It is built from "i" (in) and "princippet" (the principle). To say something is possible on paper but add a problem, follow it with "men" (but): "I princippet kan jeg komme, men jeg har travlt" (In principle I can come, but I am busy).

i sidste ende.explanation: "I sidste ende" means "in the end". To say what decides things after everything else is considered, say: "Jeg hører på alle, men i sidste ende bestemmer jeg selv" (I listen to everyone, but in the end I decide myself). For the last step in a series, use "til sidst" (at the very end): "Til sidst tager vi opvasken" (At the very end, we do the dishes).

i skole.explanation: "I skole" means "in school". To say you are going there, use "skal" (am going to): "Jeg skal i skole" (I am off to school). To say you attend school as a pupil, use "at gå" (to go): "Hun går i skole i Odense" (She goes to school in Odense).

i stedet.explanation: "I stedet" means "instead". To say which thing you pick in place of something just mentioned, put it at the end: "Vi tager bussen i stedet" (We take the bus instead). To say instead of what, use "i stedet for" (instead of): "Jeg vil have te i stedet for kaffe" (I want tea instead of coffee).

i stedet for.explanation: "I stedet for" means "instead of". Literally, it is "in the place for". To say you choose one thing and not another, say: "Jeg vil have te i stedet for kaffe" (I want tea instead of coffee). To say instead of doing something, add "at" (to) before the verb: "i stedet for at vente" (instead of waiting).

i stykker.explanation: "I stykker" means "broken". Literally, it is "in pieces". To say something has stopped working, use "er" (is): "Min cykel er i stykker" (My bike is broken). To say something broke, use "gik" (went): "Telefonen gik i stykker" (The phone broke).

i tide.explanation: "I tide" means "in time". To say you finished before a deadline, say: "Jeg afleverede opgaven i tide" (I handed in the assignment in time). Do not mix it up with "til tiden" (on time), which means at the agreed time: "Toget kom til tiden" (The train came on time).

i tilfælde af.explanation: "I tilfælde af" means "in case of". It is built from "i" (in), "et tilfælde" (a case) and "af" (of). To warn about something that might happen, say: "i tilfælde af brand" (in case of fire). To follow it with a whole sentence, add "at" (that): "Tag en paraply med i tilfælde af at det regner" (Bring an umbrella in case it rains).

i udlandet.explanation: "I udlandet" means "abroad". To say where you live, put "i" (in) before it: "Jeg bor i udlandet" (I live abroad). To say where you are going, use "til" (to): "Jeg rejser til udlandet" (I am traveling abroad). To say where someone comes from, use "fra" (from): "Han kommer fra udlandet" (He comes from abroad).

i virkeligheden.explanation: "I virkeligheden" means "in reality". It is built from "i" (in) and "virkeligheden" (the reality). To say the truth differs from how things look, say: "Det ser nemt ud, men i virkeligheden er det svært" (It looks easy, but in reality it is hard).

i weekenden.explanation: "I weekenden" means "this weekend / on the weekend". To talk about the coming weekend, say: "Vi skal i biografen i weekenden" (We are going to the movies this weekend). To talk about the weekend just gone, use the past tense: "Jeg var i Aarhus i weekenden" (I was in Aarhus last weekend). To say how you spend every weekend, say: "Jeg sover længe i weekenden" (I sleep late on weekends).

i år.explanation: "I år" means "this year". Literally, it is "in year". To say something repeats each year, use "hvert år" (every year): "Vi rejser hvert år" (We travel every year).

i øvrigt.explanation: "I øvrigt" means "by the way". To add a side remark about something already said, say: "Bogen er god. Den er i øvrigt billig." (The book is good. It is also cheap, by the way.)

iblandt.explanation: "Iblandt" means "among". It is built from "i" (in) and "blandt" (among). The shorter word "blandt" means the same: "Hun er blandt de bedste" (She is among the best).

ideel.explanation: "Ideel" means "ideal". The noun is "et ideal" (an ideal). To say something is perfect for a purpose, add "til" (for) and the purpose: "Huset er ideelt til en stor familie" (The house is ideal for a big family).

identisk.explanation: "Identisk" means "identical". To say two things are exactly the same, add "med" (with) and the other thing: "Svaret er identisk med mit" (The answer is identical to mine). The Danish word ends in "-isk", not "-ical".

idet.explanation: "Idet" means "as". Literally, it is "i det" (in that), written as one word. To say two things happen at the same moment, say: "Idet han gik ud, slukkede han lyset" (As he went out, he turned off the light).

idræt.explanation: "Idræt" means "PE". To say what class you have at school, say: "Vi har idræt efter frokost" (We have PE after lunch). Outside school, it means "sports" as an activity: "Hun elsker idræt" (She loves sports).

ifølge.explanation: "Ifølge" means "according to". To name where the information comes from, say: "ifølge lægen" (according to the doctor). To give your own view instead, use "efter min mening" (in my opinion): "Efter min mening er filmen dårlig" (In my opinion the film is bad).

igen.explanation: "Igen" means "again". To say you will return, say: "Jeg kommer igen" (I will come back). To say another person is included, use "også" (too): "Jeg kommer også" (I am coming too).

igennem.explanation: "Igennem" means "through". The shorter word "gennem" means the same: "gennem skoven" (through the forest). To say you read or check something from start to finish, put "igennem" after the verb: "Jeg læste bogen igennem" (I read the book all the way through).

ikke.explanation: "Ikke" means "not". To say something is not so, put it after "er" (is): "Det er ikke dyrt" (It is not expensive). Do not mix it up with "nej" (no), which answers a question: "Nej, jeg er ikke sulten" (No, I am not hungry).

ikke desto mindre.explanation: "Ikke desto mindre" means "nevertheless". Literally, it is "not the less". To say something is still true despite what was just said, say: "Det var dyrt. Ikke desto mindre købte vi det" (It was expensive. Nevertheless, we bought it).

ikke endnu.explanation: "Ikke endnu" means "not yet". To answer a question about being ready, say: "Er du klar?" "Ikke endnu." (Are you ready? Not yet.) To say you have not done something so far, put "endnu" (yet) at the end: "Jeg har ikke ringet endnu" (I have not called yet). Do not mix it up with "ikke mere" (not anymore), which says something has stopped: "Jeg bor ikke her mere" (I do not live here anymore).

ikke engang.explanation: "Ikke engang" means "not even". To say something is missing although you would expect it, say: "Hun har ikke engang tid til en kop kaffe" (She does not even have time for a cup of coffee). The part "engang" also appears in the fairy-tale opening "Der var engang" (Once upon a time).

ikke mere.explanation: "Ikke mere" means "no more". To turn down more of something, say: "Mere kaffe?" "Nej tak, ikke mere." (More coffee? No thank you, no more.) To say something has stopped, it means "not anymore": "Jeg bor ikke her mere" (I do not live here anymore).

ild.explanation: "Ild" means "fire", as in flames. Do not mix it up with "en brand" (a destructive fire): "Der er brand i huset" (The house is on fire). To ask someone for a light, say: "Har du ild?" (Do you have a light?)

ilt.explanation: "Ilt" means "oxygen". To say a patient is given oxygen, say: "Patienten får ilt" (The patient is getting oxygen). Do not mix it up with "ild" (fire), which differs by one letter: "Man må ikke lege med ild" (You must not play with fire).

imellem.explanation: "Imellem" means "between". To say something sits in the space of two things, say: "imellem to huse" (between two houses). To say something happens from time to time, use "en gang imellem" (once in a while): "Jeg ser hende en gang imellem" (I see her once in a while).

imens.explanation: "Imens" means "while". It is built from "i" (in) and "mens" (while). To say what happens during the wait, start a second sentence with it, where it means "meanwhile": "Jeg laver mad. Imens dækker du bord" (I am cooking. Meanwhile you set the table).

immunitet.explanation: "En immunitet" means "an immunity". To say someone cannot catch an illness, add "mod" (against): "Hun har immunitet mod influenza" (She has immunity to the flu). In law, the word means protection from prosecution: "diplomatisk immunitet" (diplomatic immunity).

imod.explanation: "Imod" means "against". To say you play against someone, say: "Vi spiller imod dem" (We play against them). To say you move toward something, it means "toward": "Hun gik imod døren" (She walked toward the door).

imponerende.explanation: "Imponerende" means "impressive". It comes from the verb "at imponere" (to impress). To talk about the person who feels it, use "imponeret" (impressed): "Jeg er imponeret" (I am impressed).

imponeret.explanation: "Imponeret" means "impressed". It comes from the verb "at imponere" (to impress). To say what impressed you, add "over" (about): "Jeg er meget imponeret over resultatet" (I am very impressed with the result). Do not mix it up with "imponerende" (impressive), which describes the thing that impresses: "et imponerende resultat" (an impressive result).

import.explanation: "En import" means "an import". It is the noun for the verb "at importere" (to import). To talk about goods leaving the country, use the opposite, "en eksport" (an export): "Firmaet lever af eksport" (The company lives off export).

impulsiv.explanation: "Impulsiv" means "impulsive". It comes from the noun "en impuls" (an impulse). To say you bought something without planning, say: "Det var et impulskøb" (It was an impulse buy).

ind.explanation: "Ind" means "in". To tell someone to come into a room, say: "Kom ind!" (Come in!) To say the place you enter, add "i" (in) after it: "Hun løber ind i butikken" (She runs into the store). To say someone is already inside, use "inde" (inside): "Han er inde" (He is inside).

indadvendt.explanation: "Indadvendt" means "introverted". It is built from "indad" (inward) and "vendt" (turned), so it means "turned inward". To describe someone who likes meeting people, use the opposite, "udadvendt" (outgoing): "Hun er meget udadvendt" (She is very outgoing).

indbydende.explanation: "Indbydende" means "inviting". It comes from the verb "at indbyde" (to invite). To say something looks tempting, say: "Vandet så indbydende ud" (The water looked inviting).

indefra.explanation: "Indefra" means "from the inside". To say where a lock is, say: "Døren er låst indefra" (The door is locked from the inside). To say from the outside, use the opposite, "udefra": "Døren kan kun åbnes udefra" (The door can only be opened from the outside).

inden.explanation: "Inden" means "before". To say something happens before a time, put the time after it: "Vi er hjemme inden middag" (We are home before dinner). Do not mix it up with "indenfor" (inside), which is about a place: "Vi er indenfor" (We are inside).

indenfor.explanation: "Indenfor" means "inside". To invite someone in from the door, say: "Kom indenfor!" (Come in!) To say within a time, say: "indenfor en uge" (within a week).

indeni.explanation: "Indeni" means "inside". To say what the inside of a thing is like, say: "Æblet er råddent indeni" (The apple is rotten inside). To talk about feelings you hide, say: "Hun smiler, men hun er ked af det indeni" (She smiles, but she is sad inside).

indenlandsk.explanation: "Indenlandsk" means "domestic". It is built from "inden" (within) and "land" (country). To talk about goods from another country, use the opposite, "udenlandsk" (foreign): "udenlandske varer" (foreign goods).

inderst.explanation: "Inderst" means "at the very back". It is the "most" form of "indre" (inner). To talk about true feelings, use "inderst inde" (deep down): "Inderst inde er han bange" (Deep down he is afraid).

indflydelsesrig.explanation: "Indflydelsesrig" means "influential". It is built from "indflydelse" (influence) and "rig" (rich), so it means "rich in influence". To say who is affected, add "på" (on) after "indflydelse": "Han har stor indflydelse på sine kolleger" (He has great influence on his colleagues).

indfødsret.explanation: "En indfødsret" means "a citizenship". It is built from "indfødt" (native) and "ret" (right). In Denmark, a new citizen is granted "indfødsret" by a law passed in parliament.

indfødt.explanation: "Indfødt" means "native", as in born in a place: "en indfødt københavner" (a native Copenhagener). It is built from "ind" (in) and "født" (born).

indhold.explanation: "Indholdet" means "the content". It comes from the verb "at indeholde" (to contain). The list at the front of a book is "en indholdsfortegnelse" (a table of contents).

indien.explanation: "Indien" means "India". To say a person is from India, use "en inder" (an Indian person): "Han er inder" (He is an Indian). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Hun er indianer" (She is a Native American).

indimellem.explanation: "Indimellem" means "now and then". It is built from "ind" (in) and "imellem" (between). To say someone does something from time to time, say: "Hun ringer indimellem" (She calls now and then).

indisk.explanation: "Indisk" means "Indian", from "Indien" (India). To talk about a person from India, use "en inder" (an Indian person). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Han er indianer" (He is a Native American).
